title: Geo-AI mapping reveals contrasting land cover and heat patterns across four Indonesian cities
summary: A Research Square preprint used Random Forest classification of 2025 satellite imagery to compare land cover, surface temperature and topographic wetness in four Indonesian cities. It found built-up land dominated Surakarta and Yogyakarta, while vegetation dominated Padang and Malang; Yogyakarta had the highest mean surface temperature in the analyzed scenes. Classification was checked using 200 higher-resolution-image reference points, with reported overall accuracy of 92.5–94.5%. These snapshot associations do not establish causal urban-heating effects or observed benefits from the proposed green-space planning recommendations.
organization: University of Brawijaya; Andalas University; State University of Malang; Bandung Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Random Forest land-cover classification compared with 200 reference points from higher-resolution Google satellite imagery (50 per class); overall accuracy 92.5–94.5% and Kappa 90–93%. LULC classifications were combined with Landsat surface temperature and SRTM-based TWI analyses for four Indonesian cities using 2025 imagery.
evidence.unknown: Only four cities and 2025 scenes were analyzed; validation used 50 reference points per land-cover class. The proposed green-space allocation and heat/runoff implications have not been validated through observed planning or intervention outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Random Forest classification provides the land-cover maps used to quantify urbanization and compare those patterns with satellite-derived surface temperature and terrain wetness across four cities.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced original Research Square v1 full PDF/text: posting metadata, affiliations, learned operation, validation design, reported result and limitations.
